scenario_prompt: Write a short demo script for a live discovery session, showing the specific capability the buyer asked to see rather than a generic product tour. Context: the buyer's VP of Infrastructure said in discovery he wants 'a perimeter we can actually govern,' referring to replacing manual failover across a 620-virtual-machine on-premises estate. The demo should show a governed project perimeter being applied to a representative workload on the target cloud platform. Return only the demo script text.
text:
**Demo or discovery material**

Customer source material for this task: the VP of Infrastructure's discovery statement, "a perimeter we can actually govern," referring to manual failover across the 620-VM on-premises estate. I'm treating this quote as supplied source material; no other discovery notes or figures were provided, so every other number below is either marked as a gap or left to you to fill from the account record.

---

**Opening (before the screen share)**

You told us you want "[PF-3.3: customer's term, retained — discovery call, VP of Infrastructure] a perimeter we can actually govern" — right now, failover across your 620-VM estate is a manual process your team runs by hand. Today I'll show you that governed perimeter applied to one representative workload, live, on [PF-1.9: target cloud platform — name the platform here].

**Segment 1 — Define the perimeter (3 min)**

I'm creating a single project-level boundary around one representative VM workload from your estate. Watch what happens as I attach it: the policies you'd need — network isolation, IAM scope, failover rules — apply to everything inside this boundary the moment it's created, not as a separate step afterward.

*[Create the project, attach the workload]*

That's the perimeter. Nothing enters or leaves it without the rule set you just watched get applied.

**Segment 2 — Trigger a failover inside the perimeter (5 min)**

Today, when a VM fails in your estate, someone finds it, someone routes around it, by hand. I'm going to simulate a failure on this workload now.

*[Trigger simulated failure]*

Watch the perimeter: failover executes according to the policy attached to the project, not a runbook someone opens. No one on my side is touching a console during this step.

[PF-1.13/PF-1.14: your current mean-time-to-failover across the 620-VM estate — GAP: no baseline was supplied; if you can give us that figure and its source, we'll show the delta against this workload's failover time live in the same demo]

**Segment 3 — Show the governance surface (4 min)**

This is the part your infra team will actually live in day to day: one view showing every policy attached to this perimeter, every workload inside it, and every change made to it.

*[Open the governance/policy dashboard]*

If you expand this estate from one workload to your full 620, this is the same view — one perimeter definition, not 620 individual configurations to keep in sync by hand.

[PF-1.17 GAP: a named, checkable reference customer running this pattern at comparable VM-estate scale was not supplied — if you have one you can name, we'll bring their proof point to the next session]

**Close**

That's the perimeter you described: one governed boundary, one failover policy, applied to a workload the way it would apply across your estate. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): confirm before this ships to the buyer whether "applied across your estate" implies a migration timeline or scope commitment we haven't agreed to] Next step, if useful: we scope what governing the full 620-VM estate under this same perimeter model would look like, using your own failover numbers once you can share them.

---

## Unresolved before this document is sent

|---|---|---|
| [PF-3.3: customer's term, retained — discovery call, VP of Infrastructure] | PF-3.3 | Confirm "a perimeter we can actually govern" is accurately attributed to this discovery call before reuse. |
| [PF-1.9: target cloud platform — name the platform here] | PF-1.9 | Name of the target cloud platform to insert. |
| [PF-1.13/PF-1.14 GAP: no baseline was supplied] | PF-1.13, PF-1.14 | Buyer's current mean-time-to-failover across the 620-VM estate, and its source. |
| [PF-1.17 GAP: no named reference customer supplied] | PF-1.17 | A named, checkable reference running this pattern at comparable scale, if one exists and disclosure is confirmed. |
